# The one path

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

A product builder's whole road: these commands, in this order, from [day zero](day-zero.md). The territory is `apps/`, `frontend/` and their derived files — among them your apps' rows in `quality/budgets.yaml` and your drawer `quality/local/`, which `scaffold` and `rung_tidy.sh` write for you; commit them with the app. A pull request inside that territory, the drawer and `scripts/local/` included, forces no CI path onto the platform's full lane (`quality/djb/scope.py:2076`). A script of your own lives in `scripts/local/`, and its row in `docs/product/instruments.local.md`.

0. [Day zero](day-zero.md) — declare the clone a product, the first gate, the remotes, the first push; then a local admin and tenant:
   - `uv run python manage.py seed` — a laptop's tenant `acme`, `owner@example.com`, `member@example.com` and an API token printed once; DEBUG only, and a second run is another token
   - `uv run python manage.py issue_token --email <email> --tenant <slug> --name <label> --scope '*'` — a token for the machine door (REST, MCP), printed once; narrow `--scope` to the job
   - `uv run python manage.py zitadel_first_admin --email <you>` — a deployment's first human: the link where they set their own password; refused once a tenant exists
   - `uv run python manage.py bootstrap_tenant --email <you>` — after that first sign-in: the installation's first tenant, with you its owner
   - `uv run python manage.py grant_staff --email <email> --as <a superuser's email>` — staff (opens `/admin/`), audited; the road that replaces `createsuperuser`
1. `./scripts/setup.sh` — a fresh clone to a running checkout; it ends with `next: uv run python manage.py scaffold --list`
2. `uv run python manage.py newapp <app>` — a fresh app under `apps/` (registered by its `apps.py`, nothing else), printing its `undo:` line and a `wrote:` line for the app map it rewrote in your `docs/product/architecture.md`, which the app's commit carries. Name it for the collection its nouns belong to, never a noun's own plural: `newapp workorders` holds the noun `Job` the way `example` holds `Widget`; `newapp jobs` then `scaffold noun jobs Job` is refused by house rule 32, because the copy would mount at `/jobs/`, which is an app label (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:331`)
3. `uv run python manage.py roads shape <shape> <app> <Noun>` — what the shape would write, before it writes (`scaffold --dry-run`)
4. `uv run python manage.py scaffold <shape> <app> <Noun>` — the golden copied onto your noun, renamed; it ends with `next:`
5. `./scripts/feature.sh <app>` — makemigrations, tidy, the `--fast` gate, this checkout's database migrated, then the app's own tests (`test.sh apps/<app>`) — green, or the first red `file:line`. Green means `serve.sh` and `worker.sh` meet a migrated database and the app's tests pass; the apps that depend on it run in the loop (step 8) (`quality/djb/rituals/feature.py:144`, `quality/djb/rituals/feature.py:147`)
6. `./scripts/feature.sh <app> --drive <Noun>` — before the gate, a preflight: the server answers, it serves this checkout's database, and the seed rows exist; then the road (step 5's, the checkout migrated and the app's tests run) and the doors driven live — REST, MCP, the PATCH, the event and every verb the noun declares, pressed once; `doors agree` or the first differing key (`quality/djb/rituals/feature.py:140`, `quality/djb/rituals/drive_doors.py:469`)
7. `uv run python manage.py scaffold screen <Noun>` — the face for the noun, once `feature.sh` has regenerated the published document: its screens, client calls and words under `frontend/`, every file printed, ending with `Next:` naming the product's two pages it wrote. The product's pages land at `frontend/src/app/<page>/` (`page.tsx` and `[id]/page.tsx`), and a page of your own goes there too; the noun's dev-only walk pages land under `frontend/src/app/example/<page>/`, the prefix the face's route table declares for walks (`WALK_PREFIX` in `frontend/src/kit/routes.ts`, a table `scaffold screen` grows, so the page names it without a line), and yield to your pages. `frontend/src/app/example/` and `apps/example*` are the template's worked example, which a product copies from and then deletes (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/screen.py:360`)
8. `./scripts/feature.sh <app> --loop --here "<app>: <why>"` — the per-rung loop: every leg, every red named. On a laptop the gate refuses a `--loop` without `--here` and its reason (`<app>: <why>`); a verifier box needs none
9. `./scripts/take_release.sh <tag>` — a new platform release folded in from the `template` remote (`--remote <name>` names another): fetch, census, merge, fold, the SDK step, the base recorded (`scripts/local/template-base` = the tag taken; commit it with the release), the gate. Then run `uv run python manage.py declare <ns>` again to move the rule ceiling

## What `scaffold` writes outside `apps/<app>/`

Everything a shape writes is under `apps/<app>/`, except these:

- `quality/budgets.yaml` — your app's budget rows, measured by the tidy; `scaffold` writes only rows under `apps/<app>/` and leaves every other row as it was; commit them with the app (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:67`)
- `apps/conftest_local.py` — the fixtures drawer: your door-parity test modules added to its population addend; commit it (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:72`)
- `quality/local/frozen_families.yaml` — your noun's scope families, frozen on a declared product (`declare <ns>` makes it one); commit it (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:79`)
- `apps/core/api/frozen_families.py` — the template's own frozen-family census: written on the undeclared template only, never by a product's `scaffold`, which sends them to the drawer above; the hook refuses a product commit to it (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:65`)
- `docs/product/architecture.md` — your own decision page: its app map is a derived block over every `apps/*/apps.py` and door file, and `newapp` and each `scaffold` write rewrite it, printing a `wrote:` line per block; commit it with the app, or the hook refuses the stale block (`apps/core/scaffold/arms/_common.py:81`)
- `frontend/**` — `scaffold screen` writes only there: the noun's screens, its client calls, its words and its rows in the face's shared tables
